report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of daedalus/eval/ceiling.py: per-task classification, summary/ceiling computation, render_ceiling, and main. Claims verified, no defects found.

handoff.purpose: Finalize per-task classification, compute summaries and ceilings, render output, and CLI entrypoint.

symbols.name: _def_count
symbols.note: Defines a closure count_of that sums counts over sorted aliases for a given arm revision.

symbols.name: count_of
symbols.note: Closure returned by _def_count; returns sum of counts for all aliases of a definition.

symbols.name: _summary
symbols.note: Aggregates per-task class values into a sorted count dict for a given key ('classes_clean' or 'classes_leaky').

symbols.name: _ceiling
symbols.note: Returns REACHABLE count divided by denominator, or 0.0 if denominator is zero.

symbols.name: render_ceiling
symbols.note: Builds an ASCII-only report string from the result dict, including summaries, ceilings, static-edge warnings, reachable labels, notes, and reopen signal.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: CLI entrypoint: parses --min-count, calls temporal_ceiling, renders, prints with ASCII fallback.

claims.why: All literal strings are ASCII; the UnicodeEncodeError fallback in main confirms the ASCII-only intent.

claims.text: None parents == probe failed / no sha; [] cannot happen for a resolvable sha (a root commit yields [''] -> filtered to []).
claims.why: The code assigns backtest_rev_reason based on has_rev and sha; the comment describes the data invariant, which is consistent with the logic shown.

claims.text: The lane A2 reopen trigger, stated by the machine so a future session cannot misread the close: the clean rename-aware ceiling must clear the materiality floor (share OR breadth), not merely be non-zero -- the 2026-07-21 close measured exactly one recoverable label, and one label must read as 'stay closed' (see REOPEN_MIN_* rationale).
claims.why: reopen_temporal_lane is computed as ceiling_clean >= REOPEN_MIN_SHARE or n_tasks_reachable_clean >= REOPEN_MIN_TASKS, matching the claim. The historical note is uncheckable but the logic matches.

claims.text: min_count=2; 1 = most permissive ceiling, any single prior co-commit.
claims.why: The help string explicitly states default 2 and that 1 is the most permissive; this matches the code.

claims.text: The gap between the two arms is the self-prediction artifact: coupling that exists only because the minted commit is counted.
claims.why: The leaky arm includes the mint commit while clean arm excludes it; the comment accurately describes the gap.

claims.text: STATIC_EDGE misses present: a missed label's defining file is ALREADY a static neighbour of the focus. That is edge-but-dropped -- a slicer defect, strictly more important than anything temporal.
claims.why: The code detects STATIC_EDGE in summaries and prints the warning and lists affected tasks.

claims.text: clean-arm REACHABLE labels (audit these -- each is a claim that pre-mint history named the file).
claims.why: The code collects and prints REACHABLE labels from classes_clean, matching the claim.

claims.text: note: {id} minted at a MERGE commit; clean arm is first-parent history only.
claims.why: The code prints this note when merge_commit is true.

claims.text: note: {id} has no backtest rev ({reason}); clean arm not scored.
claims.why: The code prints this note when backtest_rev_reason is truthy.

claims.text: rename-alias probe(s) failed: those files were scored rename-BLIND and the ceiling may be understated.
claims.why: The code prints this warning when alias_probe_failures is truthy.

claims.text: REOPEN signal: clean rename-aware ceiling clears the materiality floor ({floor}) -- the temporal-enrichment lane may be worth reopening (see module docstring).
claims.why: The code prints this when reopen_temporal_lane is true.

claims.text: ...measured at min_count=1, BELOW the reopen threshold: a single co-occurrence is one data point, not a pattern (churn.py). The reopen condition is defined at min_count >= 2.
claims.why: The code prints this when min_count < 2 and reopen_temporal_lane is true.

claims.text: reopen signal: none -- N clean-reachable label(s) in M task(s) is below the materiality floor ({floor}); the temporal lane stays closed.
claims.why: The code prints this when not reopen_temporal_lane but n_reach > 0.

claims.text: reopen signal: none -- clean ceiling is zero; the temporal lane stays closed.
claims.why: The code prints this when n_reach is zero and reopen_temporal_lane is false.

observations.what: The leaky arm classification uses _def_count(leaky_counts, None) and includes the minted commit, while the clean arm uses _def_count(clean_counts, rev) excluding it. This matches the documented self-prediction artifact.
The ceiling_clean denominator is n_scored_clean (labels excluding NO_BACKTEST_REV), while ceiling_leaky uses n_labels. This is consistent with the clean arm not being scored for some tasks.
The reopen signal uses REOPEN_MIN_SHARE and REOPEN_MIN_TASKS constants defined elsewhere in the module; the comment explains the rationale.
